observation: Round 2 changed the detected-line visualization but did not escape fallback: real-detection ratio stayed 0, fallback stayed 1, and the prompt count, fill rate, completeness, segment-size CV, and ontology divergence were effectively unchanged. Its proxy fell from 0.7522 to 0.7455, so the relaxed detection settings add noise without downstream benefit. The round-1 unfolding geometry remains healthy at 3.1 cm residual and 10.8% depth NaNs; the remaining intrinsic weakness is SAM mask imbalance (segment-size CV 0.715) with only 0.565 fill and 0.9 ring completeness.
failure_mode: The detection fallback is stable but unresponsive to bounded Hough relaxation, while the SAM template appears to under-cover its narrow K region relative to the other circumferential blocks, contributing to uneven mask sizes and incomplete lining coverage.
rationale: Revert all ineffective round-2 detection changes, retain the proven unfolding correction, and isolate one moderate SAM geometry adjustment. Raising K_height from the T3 prior neighborhood toward 900 mm enlarges the narrow K template without changing ring spacing, taper, denoising, or prompt generation; this directly tests whether template under-coverage drives the high segment-size variation while keeping attribution clean.
